FOREWORD "I-his Indian Standard ( Second Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Copper and Copper Alloys Sectional Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council, `This standard was first published in 1975 and subsequently revised in 1985. The phosphor bronze are commonly used for deep drawing into bellows, stamping and forming into spring devices and into terminals and connectors for electrical apparatus, because they combine high strength with high elongation. in this standard following a) b) c) d) modifications have been made:

One more grade has been added. Relevant chemical composition Drawings and mechanical properties for the new grade have been incorporated.

for the bend test have been added. of tolerances have been incorporated in the standard. of this standard is complied with, the final value,

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the \atest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards : Monthly Additions'.
